51.O. Whistle-blower disclosure.- (1) Any person making a whistle-blower 
disclosure shall make a personal declaration that the information disclosed and 
allegations contained therein are true to the best of his knowledge and belief, and 
are not disclosed for any personal reason.

(2) 
Every whistle-blower disclosure shall be made in writing or electronic 
form in such manner and accompanied by such documents or other material as may 
be prescribed.

(3) 
Upon receipt of whistle-blower disclosure, the Investigating Officer or 
any other authorized officer shall make an assessment of the information contained 
in the disclosure and verify the same under intimation to the next higher authority in 
such manner as may be prescribed.

(4)       Upon assessment and verification under sub-section (3), if the 
Investigating Officer or officer is of the view that the whistle-blower disclosure 
warrants further probe, inquiry or investigation, he shall complete such probe 
immediately but not later than twenty-four hours and take necessary action, if so 
required.

51.P. Reward and punishment.- (1) If any violation or offence is determined by the 
Investigating Officer or any officer on whistle-blower’s disclosure and offender is 
punished in consequence of such disclosure, such whistle-blower may be rewarded 
in addition to a certificate of appreciation, as may be prescribed:

Provided that in case of disclosures by more than one whistle-blower for the 
same violation or offence, reward shall equally be distributed amongst such whistle-
blowers based on their respective contribution, as determined by the Director 
General (Forests).

(2) In case a whistle-blower discloses such information which is false, 
frivolous or vexatious and on such disclosure, Investigating Officer or Director 
General (Forests) or authorized officer, after making probe on it and by providing an

opportunity of hearing, the said whistle blower shall be liable to fine which may 
extend up to one hundred thousand rupees.

51.Q. Protection of whistle-blower.- (1) The identity of a whistle-blower, other 
than provided in sub-section (2) of section 51-O, shall not be disclosed even after 
conclusion of proceedings except with written consent of such whistle-blower and in 
case an unauthorized disclosure of identity of such whistle-blower has been made 
by an officer or official, it shall deemed to be a misconduct under the Punjab 
Employees Efficiency, Discipline and Accountability Act, 2006 (XII of 2006).

(2) 
The Director General (Forests) may, in consultation with whistle-
blower, take necessary measure for his protection for such duration and in such 
manner as may be prescribed.]
